title: Who Gets Recommended? Investigating Gender, Race, and Country Disparities in Paper Recommendations from Large Language Models

bias_targets.methodology: Comparing the citation counts of LLM-recommended papers against expert-curated baselines of important papers to measure the Matthew effect.
Predicting the gender of LLM-recommended scholars using name-based algorithmic tools (e.g., sexmachine, nltk, gender-guesser) and comparing the distribution to real-world baselines.
Predicting the race of LLM-recommended scholars using algorithmic tools (e.g., Surgeo, Ethnicolr) and comparing the racial distribution to real-world academic baselines.

Classifying the institutional affiliations of recommended authors into developed versus developing countries using the Human Development Index (HDI) and comparing these geographic distributions to actual baselines.
